_what_this_is: Sources the DMZ fetch worker (scripts/openclaw_axis_worker.py) may reach.
One entry = one URL, one path into its JSON, one axis+key it feeds.
THIS FILE IS THE ALLOWLIST. The worker fetches nothing that is not named
here, so widening what CORTEX reaches from the outside world is a human
edit to a config file, not a decision a model can make at runtime.
_the_contract: Whatever the path resolves to must be a finite number. A string, a null, a
list, a bool — all refused, by name, into external_refusals.jsonl. The
number is what crosses the boundary; nothing else does.
_data_date_path: OPTIONAL, and only where the payload REALLY carries the reading's own date.
It is walked with the same dotted syntax as `path` and goes onto the card as
`data_date`, the spelling config/field_names.json already registers for this
concept. A source without one produces a card whose data_date is null and
which says why: the fetch time is the date of the REQUEST, not of the
reading, and a card carrying it would claim a month-old figure was observed
MEASURED 20 September 2026 by fetching all four bodies once, read-only.
Exactly one carries a date for the number being read. The other three say
so in `_data_date_why` rather than being given an invented path.
_path_syntax: Dotted keys walk objects. Integer segments index lists.
'#len' takes the length of the list at that point.

sources.why: seismometer network — instrument record, no interested party
sources._data_date_why: NONE, measured 20 Sep 2026. The whole body is {"count":13,"maxAllowed":20000} — 31 bytes, no date anywhere. The observation window lives in the URL (starttime=now-1days) and not in the answer, so there is nothing to walk to. The card's data_date stays null with its reason.

MEASURED 20 Sep 2026: the body carries {"current":{"time":"2026-09-20T12:15","interval":900,"temperature_2m":27.3}}. `current.time` sits in the SAME object as the value `path` reads and is the timestamp OF that reading — current_units.time says iso8601 and current.interval says the reading covers 900 seconds. This is the one seed source whose payload dates its own number.

NONE THAT FITS THE VALUE, measured 20 Sep 2026. Every element carries its own EPOCH (e.g. '2026-09-19T20:52:34.435200'), but `path` here is '#len' — the value is the COUNT of objects over the window the URL names (GROUP=last-30-days), and a count has no single observation date. Declaring .0.EPOCH would date the count by whichever object happens to be first in the list, which is a different fact wearing the right shape. Null with a reason is the honest card.
NOT APPLICABLE: this source is meant to refuse, so it never produces a value to date.
sources.why: DELIBERATELY BROKEN. The endpoint is real and answers 200; the path walks into a number as if it were an object. Kept in the allowlist on purpose so the refusal path is exercised on every run instead of only in a test.
